controls.label: Albedo
controls.notes: The low-phase PolyCam mosaic is normalized with the ROLO phase function and Lommel–Seeliger disk function. Its 6.25 cm source sampling covers approximately ±55° latitude. The publisher’s 8-bit stretch maps 0.002–0.007 to 1–254. Gray grid marks source NoData, including the polar gaps.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: The 5 cm global image basemap retains surface texture and photographed shading. It was normalized to 30° phase and registered to the SPC v28 control shape; small differences from the OLA v20 display mesh remain. This is a separate observed image view; it does not silently fill the albedo view’s missing poles.

controls.label: Reflected light
controls.notes: MapCam 473 nm normal reflectance from the USGS 25 cm v2 release, corrected with the published ROLO model. Grayscale maps 0–0.08 I/F to black–white for all four bands. Valid negative values remain data and clip to black; values above 0.08 clip to white. Gray grid marks native missing samples, including the poles. The 250 m map reference sphere does not rescale the existing 241 m OLA v20 display shape; individual boulders may not align exactly.

controls.label: Spectral color
controls.notes: Published MapCam false-color composite over 550 nm normal reflectance. Red shows the 847/550 nm ratio, green the 698 nm band strength, and blue the 473/550 nm ratio. These colors show spectral differences, not natural color or mineral abundance. Coverage extends to about 65° north and south; omitted shadows and gaps use the gray grid. The controlled map is draped on the simplified OLA shape, so individual boulders need not align precisely.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.notes: Color shows radius minus a 241 m reference sphere, including the body's broad irregular shape. This is not gravitational height or an image observation. Brightness adds cartographic relief from the full source model; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting. Fine terrain is represented in the map while the displayed silhouette is simplified. Values follow the nearest corresponding point on the full source shape within the display mesh’s simplification allowance. This is radial height, not gravitational height; flat previews withhold overlapping radial surfaces.

controls.label: Geopotential height

legend.title: Geopotential height
legend.meta: m above the lowest surface potential

controls.notes: Height above the lowest point of Bennu’s surface potential, as archived by the OSIRIS-REx altimetry team for OLA shape v20 at 1.68 m facets: (U − Umin)/|g|, with uniform density 1194 kg/m³ and Bennu’s spin. Material would move from high to low values. Shown on its own archived mesh; each facet keeps its released value.

controls.label: Slope
controls.notes: Angle between each facet and the local gravity plus spin acceleration, as archived for OLA shape v20 at 1.68 m facets with uniform density 1194 kg/m³. Values above 80° display at the top color. Shown on its own archived mesh; each facet keeps its released value.

controls.label: Gravity anomaly
controls.notes: Radio Science Working Group map: measured surface acceleration minus the acceleration of a uniform-density Bennu, as a percentage. Positive is stronger than uniform density. The field comes from tracked ejected particles and spacecraft. Shown on the SPC v42 mesh the product was computed on.

controls.label: Thermal inertia
controls.notes: OTES thermal inertia from all seven Detailed Survey stations, fitted with a thermophysical model (Rozitis et al. 2020). Low values mark porous, weak boulders. Facets the archive leaves empty show the gray grid. Shown on the SPO v34 mesh the product was computed on.

controls.label: 2.7 µm band
controls.notes: Depth of the 2.74 µm absorption of hydrated clay minerals in OVIRS spectra at 12:30 local time (Simon et al. 2020). The archive stores it as a fraction; the legend shows percent. Facets marked −9999 in the archive show the gray grid. Shown on the SPC v20 mesh the map was made on.

controls.label: 3.4 µm band
controls.notes: Area of the 3.2–3.6 µm absorption linked to organics and carbonates in OVIRS spectra at 12:30 local time (Simon et al. 2020). Larger values mean a stronger band, not a measured abundance. Facets marked −9999 in the archive show the gray grid. Shown on the SPC v20 mesh the map was made on.
